Meta.title: AFA — A sales system for your business
Meta.description: Websites and AI assistants that actually close sales. AFA builds sales systems, not just websites.

Home.subtitle: A site and an assistant that answer, follow up, and close for you — even at 2 a.m.

unanswered.title: Unanswered messages
unanswered.body: DMs and messages land, then sit — late or never answered. The buyer doesn't wait; they move to the next seller.

catalog.title: Invisible catalog
catalog.body: Your products aren't anywhere a buyer can browse and order on the spot. Every extra click is one fewer sale.

forgotten.title: Forgotten customers
forgotten.body: Someone who bought once is your likeliest next sale — but nothing brings them back.

Services.title: Three services, one sales system
Services.subtitle: Each service ships with its own live tool, so you test the claim with your own numbers on the spot.

website.title: Website & online store
website.body: A site where a buyer sees the product, trusts it, and orders in seconds.

assistant.title: AI answering assistant
assistant.body: An assistant that answers around the clock, quotes prices, and takes orders.

automation.title: Operations & customer return
automation.body: Automatic reminders and follow-ups that bring past buyers back and build recurring revenue.

prices.q: Why are there no prices on the site?
prices.a: Tools give you scope and timeline, not a number. Pricing is set in a short call, matched to your actual work.

time.a: Work ships in phases. The first usable phase reaches you well before the full build and runs from day one.

ownership.q: Who owns the code and access?
ownership.a: You do — source, domain, hosting, and every key. Nothing stays locked to us.

iran.q: Does it run reliably from Iran?
iran.a: Yes. Infrastructure, fonts, and tools are chosen to stay fast and reachable from Iran.

assistant.a: Yes — soon you'll talk to it directly on the assistant page and see for yourself.

Cta.title: Ready to build your sales system?
Cta.subtitle: One short call to map the scope and the first phase together.
